Chapter 182: 0179 President Chen, the Admissions Ambassador for the Yuanpei Program

This year, the military training for new students at Peking University was a week earlier than last year.

Perfectly missing the Top 3 competition and the finals of "Super Girl"!

It was only August 12th, and the new students had already reported in. They were heading to military training on the 15th.

In the small restaurant outside the South Gate, every seat was taken. The national Top 5 competition of "Super Girl" was about to air.

Chen Guiliang, Jiang Junlai, Xie Yang, and Yang Shuo were currently sitting at a table against the wall, eating. Beside them were all new students and their parents, chatting while staring at the TV.

"Who do you guys think will make the top five?" Jiang Junlai asked.

Yang Shuo buried his head in his food; he couldn't even recognize all the contestants.

Xie Yang said, "Li Yuchun, Zhou Bichang, Zhang Liangying, He Jie... it's hard to say for the last one."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Not bad, great minds think alike."

"I did my research," Xie Yang said.

He researched Super Girl purely for work.

The microblogging feature on Kaixinwang had long been launched, but for now, you could only post using a computer.

The WAP site, with its greatly reduced functions and page design, was scheduled for its official beta launch tomorrow. With it, people could post on their microblogs using their mobile phones.

Currently, the celebrities who had joined Kaixinwang were all used to writing long blog posts of several hundred words and didn't like posting microblogs with only a few dozen characters.

Even with the launch of the WAP site, it would probably be a while before user habits could be changed.

They had to use celebrities for promotion and guidance, turning sending and receiving microblogs on mobile phones into a new trend.

The first choice for a celebrity was, of course, Jay Chou.

But 2005 was the peak of Jay Chou's endorsement fees: his non-exclusive endorsement fee for mainland China was over 12 million yuan a year, and filming commercials cost extra.

The currently popular Super Girls were the most suitable for Kaixinwang.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Have you sent someone to find out the price for an advertising endorsement from the top three Super Girls?"

Xie Yang had already done his homework. "For a non-exclusive endorsement for similar products, the package price for the top three is 6 million for a one-year term. An exclusive endorsement would be another 2 million. Additionally, the commercial shoot is billed by the day, with a package price of 1.6 million per day for the three of them. Their commercial shooting schedule is already full, so if we want to hire them, we'll have to wait until after the competition."

"Quite expensive," Chen Guiliang said with some regret for not securing the endorsement earlier.

The problem was that before Super Girl started airing, Chen Guiliang himself was short on funds, and he wouldn't have known where to find the specific contestants anyway.

Chen Guiliang asked again, "What if we only hire the third-place winner, including the commercial shoot? What would the price be?"

Xie Yang said, "1.6 million at most, maybe we can negotiate it down to 1 million. The price range fluctuates a lot; their management company always likes to ask for the moon."

Although the competition was still ongoing, Chen Guiliang already knew who would be in third place.

Zhang Liangying, she was quite suitable for an endorsement.

The champion, Li Yuchun, was actually more controversial. Although a huge number of people liked her, just as many disliked her.

"Are we really going to ask the Super Girls to do a commercial? TV advertising fees are very expensive," Xie Yang said.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm not placing the ad on TV."

"Video websites?" Xie Yang immediately understood.

"Smart," Chen Guiliang praised.

By now, six video websites had appeared in mainland China.

They were: LeTV, Sohu Video, Tudou, 56.com, PPTV, and PPS.

These websites were gaining users every day. But aside from Sohu Video, the advertising revenue for the others was very scarce.

Take Sohu Video for example, the one with the most users and the highest prices. To run a pre-roll ad in the hit drama "Chinese Paladin," it only cost 35 yuan per 1000 impressions. The more impressions you bought at once, the cheaper the overall fee.

As for LeTV and 56.com, which barely got any ads, you could get away with paying them just a little bit.

Tudou's prices were somewhere in the middle.

Especially on video websites that were primarily UGC-based, Chen Guiliang could even upload the full-length commercial without spending a single cent. The website might even be happy about it because an ad featuring the Super Girls could potentially increase their traffic.

Hearing their conversation, Jiang Junlai was utterly shocked. "Damn, you guys are really going to hire the Super Girls for an endorsement?"

Chen Guiliang said, "The champion and runner-up are too expensive. We can only afford the third-place winner."

"That's still awesome!" Jiang Junlai said.

Xie Yang asked, "For the ad content, do we need to hire a professional advertising agency to plan it?"

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "I'll plan it myself. You find an up-and-coming director, and also a top-notch stylist."

"Okay."

Xie Yang had a professional team under him. Although his own abilities were limited, he was good at learning and listening to suggestions.

He was improving at a rapid pace.

With almost every task he completed, he showed significant growth. His theoretical knowledge didn't improve much, but his mindset and perspective were advancing.

To be honest, in terms of management and execution alone, the potential hidden within Xie Yang far surpassed that of a non-reborn Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang's advantage lay in his charisma. Even without being reborn, anyone who spent a long time with him would feel that Chen Guiliang was trustworthy. It was easy for him to gather a group of friends around him, and even followers.

Because Chen Guiliang always stepped up at critical moments. When faced with a thorny issue, he would never back down, charging ahead to get it done even if it meant getting battered and bruised.

Waking up in the early morning.

Chen Guiliang was already up and washing his face, while Jiang Junlai was still fast asleep.

As freshman year ended, this guy had started to slack off. One had to remember that last winter break, he had insisted on waking up early every day to study on his own.

"See you, I'm off to get breakfast and go to work!" Chen Guiliang said after rinsing his mouth.

Jiang Junlai replied groggily, "See you."

An unknown amount of time passed before the dorm room door was opened, and a parent walked in with their child.

The roommates were changing!

Min Wenyu and Guo Feng had moved to another dorm, replaced by two freshmen from the Yuanpei Program.

"Hello, young man," the parent spoke first.

Jiang Junlai rubbed his sleepy eyes and got up. "Sorry, I went to bed too late last night."

The parent asked, "Are you an upperclassman?"

"Yeah, a sophomore in the Yuanpei Program. My name is Jiang Junlai," Jiang Junlai said.

The freshman came over to shake his hand. "Hello, Senior Jiang, my name is Tong Zhihong. I'm from Lingnan."

The parent asked curiously, "The dorms aren't for the same year?"

Jiang Junlai explained, "The Yuanpei Program is different. After the freshmen enroll, some live with sophomores, and some live with juniors. Arts and science students are also mixed. It's to facilitate interdisciplinary and cross-year communication."

"That's a very good approach," the parent praised.

As they spoke, another freshman arrived, this one without a parent escort.

"Hello everyone, I'm Li Heng, from Zhongyuan."

"Hello."

The four of them chatted while making their beds.

Li Heng asked, "What's the name of the senior on the bunk above me?"

"Chen Guiliang," said Jiang Junlai.

"Chen Guiliang?!!!"

One parent and two freshmen exclaimed in unison.

Jiang Junlai was curious. "You all know him?"

The parent said, "When Director Zhu called my son Zhihong for admissions, he gave a detailed introduction of Chen Guiliang. Later, I even Baidu-ed Chen Guiliang's information. I felt the Yuanpei Program was indeed very impressive, so I discussed it with my son and we decided to apply for it."

Li Heng added, "Me too."

Well, wasn't that something? Chen Guiliang had no idea he had become this year's admissions ambassador for the Yuanpei Program!

Director Zhu really had a way with persuasion.

After having breakfast at the school cafeteria, Chen Guiliang pedaled his bicycle toward the company.

A car stopped at the entrance of the Science Park, and a Qingniao executive inside shouted to him, "President Chen, you're still riding a bicycle?"

Chen Guiliang smiled. "I can't very well drive here from the dorm, can I?"

"True. See you around, let's get coffee sometime."

"See you."

Chen Guiliang's battered bicycle with its six locks had already become a peculiar sight in the Peking University Science Park.

Every now and then, someone would greet him.
